title: FIPS operational risk: ctr(aes) or other FIPS-unregistered algo returns -ENOENT with no dmesg explanation
description: When FIPS enforcement is active (wolfssl loaded) and a caller requests an algo the FIPS provider does not support (e.g. ctr(aes), which is kcapi-only), the caller receives -ENOENT. The log at registry.c:311 fires only if a non-FIPS provider was in the list and got skipped. If no provider at all handles ctr(aes), the message is only from ioctl_init (line 742): 'not found — FIPS mode active; ensure a FIPS provider registers this algo'. This is not emitted in key_import or do_kdf paths if they hit the same condition. A support engineer deploying a new algo under FIPS enforcement has no guaranteed dmesg breadcrumb identifying that FIPS mode specifically caused the -ENOENT — they must cross-reference sysfs. In multi-provider FIPS deployments this becomes a binary search problem.
